traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests directly reference and satisfy docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md:
1) Core rules implementation - require-story-annotation rule: src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - Enforces @story via RuleModule with meta.type='problem', fixable:'code', clear messageId 'missingStory', schema with { scope, exportPriority }. - Uses buildVisitors(...) from src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts and shared helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts. - Scope and exportPriority come from DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES in helpers/require-story-core.ts and are passed through shouldProcessNode(...) to control which nodes are checked. - require-req-annotation rule: src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Enforces @req via RuleModule with meta.type='problem', fixable:'code', clear messageId 'missingReq', and schema mirroring require-story-annotation (scope, exportPriority, additionalProperties: false). - Shares scope/exportPriority semantics via DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES and shouldProcessNode(...) from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts. - Delegates detection and error reporting to shared helper checkReqAnnotation(...) in src/utils/annotation-checker.ts.
2) Function detection (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION) - Shared default scope of function-like constructs: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - export const DEFAULT_SCOPE = [ 'FunctionDeclaration', 'FunctionExpression', 'MethodDefinition', 'TSMethodSignature', 'TSDeclareFunction', ]; - require-story-annotation visitors (src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts): - FunctionDeclaration → helperReportMissing(...) - FunctionExpression (excluding those whose parent is MethodDefinition) → helperReportMissing(...) - MethodDefinition → helperReportMethod(...) - TSDeclareFunction → helperReportMissing(...) - TSMethodSignature → helperReportMissing(...) - ArrowFunctionExpression visitor exists but is gated by shouldProcessNode; since DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include 'ArrowFunctionExpression', unconfigured runs do NOT enforce on arrows. - require-req-annotation visitors (src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts): - FunctionDeclaration → runCheck(node) - FunctionExpression (skipping parent.type === 'MethodDefinition') → runCheck(node) - MethodDefinition → runCheck(node) - TSDeclareFunction → runCheck(node) - TSMethodSignature → runCheck(node) - Both rules therefore enforce on the same set of constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) and exclude ArrowFunctionExpression by default, matching REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION.
3) JSDoc parsing & shared strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING) - For @story: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, combined by hasStoryAnnotation(...). - These use ESLint SourceCode APIs: getJSDocComment, getCommentsBefore, plus raw text scanning via src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts. - For @req: - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts: getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments, then hasReqAnnotation(...) from src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts. - hasReqAnnotation looks at JSDoc + combined comments and, when that fails, uses linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq (same pattern as story helpers) against SourceCode. - Both rules (require-req-annotation via checkReqAnnotation and require-story-annotation via hasStoryAnnotation) rely on structured JSDoc and comment parsing built on ESLint SourceCode, satisfying REQ-JSDOC-PARSING.
4) Annotation required behaviour (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED) - require-story-annotation: - meta.docs.description: "Require @story annotations on functions...". - meta.messages.missingStory clearly instructs adding @story and references the story file, e.g. docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - reportMissing(...) and reportMethod(...) in src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts call context.report with messageId 'missingStory', and provide auto-fix/suggestions using createAddStoryFix(...) / createMethodFix(...). - require-req-annotation: - meta.docs.description: "Require @req annotations on function-like exports...". - meta.messages.missingReq: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation..." with explicit suggestion. - create(...) uses runCheck → checkReqAnnotation(...); if hasReqAnnotation returns false, reportMissing(...) in annotation-checker.ts calls context.report with messageId 'missingReq'. - Tests for REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Valid cases with @story and @implements. - Invalid cases with missing @story on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, class method, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. Each asserts messageId 'missingStory', suggestion descriptions, and expected fixed output. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Valid cases with only @req, @story+@req, and @implements. - Invalid cases: missing @req on plain functions, on functions with only @story, method definitions, TS function expressions (via withTsLanguageOptions), etc., all expecting messageId 'missingReq' and appropriate data.
5) Configurable scope & export priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY) - Shared implementation: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: isExportedNode(...), shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority). - require-story-annotation: - create(context) reads options[0] and derives scope (defaults to DEFAULT_SCOPE) and exportPriority (defaults to 'all'), then passes these into shouldProcessNode. - Schema in require-story-annotation.meta.schema[0] enforces scope and exportPriority shape (also validated in tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts). - require-req-annotation: - Options type uses DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - create(context) normalizes scope and exportPriority exactly the same way and uses shouldProcessNode(...) to gate checks. - Tests showing consistent semantics: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" tests unexported vs exported functions and exported arrow functions when exportPriority='exported'. - "require-story-annotation with scope option" tests that only FunctionDeclaration is enforced when scope=["FunctionDeclaration"], with arrow functions ignored. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Multiple [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE] and [REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY] tests: functions and methods reported/ignored correctly for exportPriority='exported' and 'non-exported'; scope=["FunctionDeclaration"] only enforces declarations. - This matches REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY for both rules.
6) TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT) - Implementation: - require-story-annotation has visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature; resolveTargetNode and report helpers know how to handle TSMethodSignature by inserting on the interface. - require-req-annotation has listeners for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature that call runCheck (and thus checkReqAnnotation). - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts explicitly mention TypeScript support in comments and logic. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - withTsLanguageOptions cases for TS declare function and TS method signature, both valid and invalid (missing @story) with expected fixes. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts: - Shared test helper rule that uses TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature to exercise checkReqAnnotation, with both valid and invalid (autofix) paths. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - runAnnotationCheckerTests(...) for TSDeclareFunction/TSMethodSignature with and without @req. - With TypeScript language options, multiple function expression cases (including exported TS FunctionExpression) are tested. - All Jest suites including these TS tests pass (see test output below).
7) Error messages & error location (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, user experience criteria) - require-story-annotation: - messages.missingStory contains function name placeholder {{name}} and explicit guidance: "must have an explicit @story annotation" plus example pointing to story file. - reportMissing(...) and reportMethod(...) compute human-readable names with extractName(...) and attach data { name, functionName } and suggestions to context.report. - require-req-annotation + annotation-checker: - messages.missingReq clearly states "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE')...". - annotation-checker.reportMissing(...) uses getNodeName(...) to derive name, sets node to id/key where possible, and populates data { name, functionName: name }. - Tests verify UX and data payload: - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: all invalid cases assert messageId 'missingReq' and data { name, functionName } for functions, methods, TS nodes, and anonymous constructs. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: invalid class method case checks data: { name: 'method', functionName: 'method' } and suggestions.
8) Error handling & edge cases (Acceptance: Error Handling) - Guards and try/catch are pervasive in detection helpers: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: hasStoryAnnotation(...) and reportMissing/reportMethod are wrapped in try/catch to avoid breaking lint runs on unusual AST/source conditions. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts: linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory guard against missing lines, loc, getText, malformed ranges, and swallow errors safely. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts: linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq all guard on missing sourceCode/loc/range and enclose text access in try/catch; hasReqAnnotation wraps advanced heuristics in try/catch and falls back to simple JSDoc/comment inspection. - Dedicated edge-case tests: - tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts and tests/rules/require-story-io-behavior.test.ts cover cases like missing source.lines, missing node.loc, missing getText, malformed ranges, and parent chains without @story, asserting correct false/true behaviour without throwing. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts verifies autofix behaviour and ensures helper can handle TS constructs.
9) Documentation (Acceptance: Documentation) - Rule documentation exists and is aligned with story: - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md: - References this story via @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Documents supported node types exactly as in REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Describes options (scope, exportPriority) and defaults consistent with implementation, including JSON schema and config examples. - Provides multiple correct/incorrect examples including TypeScript syntax. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md: - References this story with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Documents that it checks function declarations, function expressions, method definitions, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and explicitly notes that ArrowFunctionExpression is not currently checked, matching the implementation. - Describes options (scope, exportPriority) mirroring require-story-annotation, with defaults and allowed values. - Includes JS and TS examples (correct and incorrect), plus @implements examples.
10) Integration into plugin configuration (DoD: rule integrated into presets) - src/index.ts registers both rules in RULE_NAMES and thus in plugin.rules. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES defines severities including: - 'traceability/require-story-annotation': 'error' - 'traceability/require-req-annotation': 'error' - configs.recommended and configs.strict are flat configs built from TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES; both include these rules enabled as errors. - Verified by tests in tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Checks that rules object contains both 'require-story-annotation' and 'require-req-annotation'. - Asserts that configs.recommended[0].rules has both traceability/require-story-annotation and traceability/require-req-annotation set to 'error', and that strict mirrors recommended.
11) Test evidence (all passing) - Command executed (without extra reporters that caused earlier failure): - npm test -- --verbose - Jest output (excerpt relevant to this story): - PASS tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Multiple [REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED], [REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION], [exportPriority], and [scope] scenarios. - PASS tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Valid/invalid coverage for @req, @implements, FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and exportPriority/scope behavior. - PASS tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts - PASS tests/rules/require-story-core.test.ts - PASS tests/rules/require-story-io-behavior.test.ts - PASS tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts - Summary: Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total; Tests: 266 passed, 266 total; no failures.
All these concrete artifacts show that the specified ESLint rules, shared helpers, documentation, configuration, and tests are present and behaving as required by docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
traceability.notes: The story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented. Both require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) while excluding arrow functions by default. They share a common scope/exportPriority model, reuse aligned JSDoc/comment parsing strategies, and support TypeScript-specific syntax via TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. Error messages are clear and include function names and actionable guidance. Edge cases and malformed or missing JSDoc/comment scenarios are handled gracefully, with extensive tests covering IO helpers and detection heuristics. Rule-level documentation exists for both rules and matches the described requirements and configuration options. The rules are included as error-level entries in the plugin’s recommended and strict presets, and all related Jest test suites pass. While the story’s DoD checkboxes in the markdown are not all manually updated, the implemented code and tests satisfy the acceptance criteria and detailed requirements, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
